cards.headline: Israeli airstrike at Nasser Hospital in Gaza kills at least six people

pages.text: An Israeli airstrike on Nasser Hospital in Khan Younis, southern Gaza, killed at least six Palestinians on November 12, 2026, according to health officials and the hospital. The strike hit the hospital's surgical wing, causing heavy damage to operating rooms, the surgical department, and intensive care units. Among those killed were a surgeon and a 13-year-old boy, according to Gaza's Education Ministry. The deceased surgeon was identified as Rezik Abushira, who was featured in the 2026 documentary “American Doctor.” The Gaza Health Ministry stated those killed included medical personnel, patients, and their companions. The Israeli military confirmed the attack, stating it targeted Muhammad Abu Ismail, the commander of Hamas’s Khan Younis brigade, and additional terrorists they said were hiding inside the hospital, though the military did not provide evidence for the claim. The strike was part of a broader series of Israeli strikes that killed 11 people in Gaza on November 12, 2026, which health officials described as the deadliest single strike since Israel’s elections. While Israel says it targets militants, the strike has drawn international condemnation from Türkiye, Spain, and the United Nations. The Palestinian refugee agency has questioned whether the territory's fragile cease-fire, which took effect in October 2025, remains meaningful following the attack.

Casualty and damage reports for the Nasser Hospital strike vary by organization. Gaza's Civil Defense initially reported six deaths and more than 20 injuries. The Gaza Health Ministry confirmed the six deaths but did not provide a specific injury count. The United Nations reported six people killed and 27 injured, while the international medical charity Medecins Sans Frontieres (MSF) reported that 52 people had been wounded. A doctor at the hospital stated that nearly 30 people were wounded in the targeted building. The United Nations expressed deep alarm, with Deputy Spokesman Farhan Haq noting that interim special coordinator for the Middle East peace process Ramiz Alakbarov called for rapid, safe, and unhindered humanitarian access, including the delivery of winter supplies and durable shelter materials. Alakbarov warned that the military operations are exacerbating suffering and jeopardizing the cease-fire. MSF described the strike as unconscionable, stating that patients and medical staff should not be killed in a place where lives should be saved. The World Health Organization has documented more than 1,050 attacks on health facilities in Gaza, causing more than 1,000 deaths, while the UN reports that more than 1,700 medical personnel have been killed in the war.

cards.headline: Two bombings in Russia kill a military officer and injure an adviser to Ukraine’s former prime minister

pages.text: Two separate vehicle bombings in Russia have resulted in the death of a military officer and the injury of an adviser to a former Ukrainian prime minister. The attacks occurred within two days of each other and are part of a series of incidents linked to the conflict between Russia and Ukraine. On November 12, 2026, a military serviceman was killed by a bomb in his vehicle in St. Petersburg, according to Russia’s Investigative Committee. The committee did not identify the victim or name any suspects. However, the Fontanka news outlet reported the victim was a colonel and stated the bomb detonated while he was driving. Fontanka claimed the device was flown from Ukraine into Russia via a balloon, hidden, and then used in the attack. The outlet further alleged the device was planted by a man working at a grocery store near the victim's apartment building acting on instructions from Ukraine’s spy agency.

In Moscow, a car bombing injured Sergei Zavorotnyi, an adviser to former Ukrainian Prime Minister Mykola Azarov. Russia’s Investigative Committee confirmed the explosion struck Zavorotnyi's car and that he was hospitalized with injuries. The committee has not identified any suspects pending a criminal inquiry. Zavorotnyi previously worked for Azarov, who served as prime minister under former Ukrainian President Viktor Yanukovych. Yanukovych, described as Moscow-friendly, was forced from office by protesters and fled to Russia in February 2014. Azarov also resides in Russia.

cards.headline: South Africa's ANC backs President Ramaphosa following worst-ever local election performance

pages.text: Leaders of South Africa's ruling African National Congress (ANC) met on November 12, 2026, to discuss the party's future after securing its worst performance in a local government election. Despite the electoral setback, ANC national spokesperson Mahlengi Bhengu-Motsiri stated that President Cyril Ramaphosa will not resign. The party's vote share dropped 15 percentage points to 31 percent in the recent local elections, a decline from the 70 percent share it once commanded when it faced no challengers. This follows a national election two years ago where the ANC lost its parliamentary majority after receiving 40 percent of the vote. To maintain control in municipalities where no party secured an outright majority, the ANC must now engage in coalition negotiations with other political parties. The National Executive Committee (NEC) is expected to receive reports on initial engagements with other parties and consider adopting a mandating guide to set the instructions for the ANC's appointed negotiations team.

The ANC's secretary-general described the election results as a “catastrophic outcome” and announced that the party would enter a period of “soul-searching” to attempt to win back the trust of the South African people. Experts and observers suggest the decline reflects long-term public frustration with several issues. Tasnim Essop, a researcher at the Society, Work and Politics Institute (SWOP) at the University of the Witwatersrand, noted that the outcome reflects a slow erosion of public confidence regarding governance, leadership, and accountability, specifically concerning basic municipal services such as water, electricity, and housing, as well as high unemployment. DW correspondent Dianne Hawker-Kalubi reported that many voters expressed frustration over the lack of basic service delivery over several years. While the ANC remains the country's largest party, opposition groups saw gains, including the Democratic Alliance (DA) in major urban centers and the uMkhonto weSizwe (MK) party, launched by former President Jacob Zuma, which performed strongly in the KwaZulu-Natal province.

cards.headline: Russia and Iran cooperate to evade US sanctions via Caspian Sea routes

pages.text: A joint assessment by the Washington-based Institute for the Study of War (ISW) and the Critical Threats Project (CTP) states that Iran and Russia are cooperating to counter United States efforts to block weapons shipments to Iran through the Caspian Sea and land routes. The study indicates that Iran has used Caspian Sea trade routes with Russia to import Russian arms both before and during the 2026 US-Israel-Iran War. This activity previously led Ukraine to strike a shipment in July 2026. According to the think tank's analysis, the Caspian Sea remains outside the reach of Western monitoring bodies, which allows sanctioned Russian cargo ships to move consignments from the ports of Astrakhan and Olya to the Iranian ports of Anzali, Nowshahr, and Amirabad. Maritime traffic data shows that these sanctioned ships switch off their Automatic Identification Systems (AIS)—a technology used to broadcast a vessel's position and identity—as they approach the shores of both countries to conceal the nature of their cargoes.

The security of these maritime routes has faced direct military action. Last summer, Ukraine's Security Service announced that long-range drones targeted two cargo ships in the Caspian Sea which, according to Kyiv, were involved in transferring military equipment between Iran and Russia. Beyond maritime shipments, Tehran and Moscow are working to expand economic and transit relations through the North-South corridor. A flagship project for both nations is the completion of the Rasht-Astara railway, which serves as the missing link in a transit route connecting Russia to ports in the Persian Gulf. Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, stated following a recent meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow that the council approved an executive agreement for the railway's construction. Rezaei also noted that the meeting included discussions regarding the construction of gas pipelines from Russia to Iran to address fuel shortages and facilitate exports to neighboring countries.

Tensions regarding northern trade routes are rising while the security situation in the Strait of Hormuz remains volatile. Observers describe the current regional environment as a “no war, no peace” situation. The public relations office of the Revolutionary Guard Navy issued a statement reporting that two “supertankers” were involved in an incident the previous night while passing through the southern route of the Strait of Hormuz. The statement claimed the vessels were brought to a halt by a “massive explosion” after they had ignored repeated warnings that the southern route was unauthorized and unsafe. According to the Guard, the two vessels were carrying a total of more than four million barrels of oil.

cards.headline: Bangladesh Bank sells approximately $200 million to stabilize foreign exchange market

pages.text: Bangladesh Bank (BB) sold a total of $201 million in the interbank market on November 12, 2026, in an effort to stabilize the foreign exchange market and contain the rising cost of the US dollar, according to three bankers who requested anonymity. The central bank's auction committee took the move to address a gap between supply and demand in the market, where foreign exchange houses were reportedly charging higher rates, a private bank treasury official said. Despite the injection of dollars, the taka weakened further in the interbank market on November 12, 2026, as the weighted average interbank exchange rate rose to Tk 124.75 per dollar from Tk 124.65 the previous day.

The US dollar has been gaining value against the taka for the past couple of months due to higher demand for settling rising import bills, specifically for fuel and essential commodities ahead of Ramadan. While the exchange rate held at Tk 122.75 per dollar for several months until the fourth week of June, the taka has been losing value against the dollar since June 28. According to the BB, the greenback was trading at Tk 123.28 in the interbank market one month ago. In September, the BB resumed selling US dollars in the market after a period of more than 14 months to meet rising demand and stabilize the market.

cards.headline: El Salvador President Nayib Bukele participates in anti-gang operation near Port-au-Prince, Haiti

pages.text: El Salvador President Nayib Bukele posted footage of attack helicopters firing on a compound near Haiti’s capital, Port-au-Prince, following his request on social media for the address of Wilson Joseph, the leader of the 400 Mawozo gang. Bukele claimed the operation, conducted alongside Haitian police, demolished Joseph’s residence and gang headquarters. While Joseph was reportedly absent, as many as 20 people were killed in the attack. This intervention represents the first overseas test of Bukele’s security model and a dramatic escalation in Haiti’s fight against organized crime. The operation comes amid a flurry of anti-gang activities in Haiti, including a drone strike by a Haitian special task force that killed Mathias Saintil, head of the “Boston” gang in Cité Soleil. Following that strike, Haitian Prime Minister Alix Didier Fils-Aimé stated on the social media platform X that there was “one less gang leader.” Erik Prince, founder of the private military firm Vectus Global, responded to the strike with “Nice shot.”

El Salvador’s involvement in Haiti is part of a broader effort through the United Nations-backed Gang Suppression Force (GSF). Authorized in 2025, the GSF is intended to assist Haitian authorities in reclaiming cities and streets from violent gangs that control large areas of the nation. El Salvador is one of six countries contributing personnel to the GSF, though the force has remained severely understaffed and has struggled to turn military operations into lasting territorial gains. While the intervention has received support from some regional leaders and pro-Bukele networks, concerns are growing regarding civilian casualties and whether military gains can result in permanent security.

cards.headline: Russian drone strike hits Kyiv hospital after SpaceX system speed restrictions

pages.text: A Russian drone strike hit the National Institute of Traumatology and Orthopedics in the Shevchenkivskyi district of central Kyiv, causing a fire and damaging the building's second floor. The strike occurred at approximately 3 a.m., near several western embassies, including the Danish and Romanian embassies. Three people were injured at the hospital, and 30 others were evacuated. One witness, Oleksandr, stated the attack narrowly missed patients as smoke billowed from the burning six-storey facility. The blast also blew out windows in nearby buildings, including the National Academy of Arts across the road. This attack follows comments from Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, who said speed restrictions on SpaceX’s Starshield system had made it more difficult for Ukraine to shoot down enemy drones. Starshield is a satellite-based communications and data system used for defense purposes. Across Ukraine, local authorities reported that Russian attacks killed nine people and injured 61 others over the past day. In the southern port city of Odesa, a separate Russian drone attack killed two people and injured five others, according to Serhii Lysak, head of the city's military administration. The strikes in Odesa damaged a private house and several vehicles. In Donetsk Oblast, regional governor Vadym Filashkin reported that four people were killed and seven others were injured, with three deaths in the city of Kramatorsk and one in Bilenkom. In Kharkiv Oblast, Governor Oleh Syniehubov stated that Russian forces hit nine settlements, injuring eight people, including an 11-year-old and two 16-year-olds. In Kherson Oblast, regional governor Oleksandr Prokudin reported that Russia targeted the city of Kherson and 34 other settlements, injuring three people. In Rivne Oblast, local authorities said Russian attacks on an apartment building injured six people, including two children. Meanwhile, Russia's Ministry of Defence reported it had intercepted 1,198 Ukrainian drones overnight across more than 15 regions, describing it as one of the largest swarms sent by Kyiv. Russian officials claimed the drones targeted oil infrastructure. In the southern Russian region of Volgograd, Governor Andrei Bocharov reported that attacks on an industrial area killed at least four people and injured two others. Unverified social media video purported to show an oil refinery in Volgograd on fire, though there was no immediate official confirmation that the refinery had been attacked. Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin stated that 467 Ukrainian drones hit the capital overnight.

cards.headline: Russia and Ukraine agree to include European nations in next round of peace talks

pages.text: Russia and Ukraine have agreed to expand the next round of peace negotiations to include European countries, according to Jared Kushner, the envoy for U.S. President Donald Trump. Kushner, who is also the president's son-in-law, announced the development late on November 12, 2026, following a meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow. U.S. envoy Steve Witkoff also confirmed to Russian state TV that European participation in the next meeting is considered a very important moment because they are viewed as partners. Kushner stated on the social media platform X that including Europe will allow talks to address broader postwar European security arrangements alongside territorial issues between Ukraine and Russia. Additionally, Kushner said Washington is working toward what would be the largest prisoner exchange of the war, which could potentially reunite thousands of people with their families.

Despite the agreement to include European nations, President Putin maintained several firm positions. He refused to soften his territorial demands and warned Europe against sending peacekeeping troops into Ukraine in the event of a peace deal, characterizing such a move as a “continuation of war.” Putin also stated that Washington must work with its European allies to determine if they want peace or war in Ukraine. Following the Moscow meeting, Kushner and Witkoff traveled to Ireland to attend a European summit and meet Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy. Zelenskyy said he was pleased with the prospect of European participation and stated that the envoys and he decided to work on an agenda regarding de-escalation and potential ceasefires. Zelenskyy expressed hope that such an agenda would be established.

cards.headline: Two men found guilty of assisting Iranian intelligence in attempts to 'eliminate' UK-based journalists

pages.text: Mostafa Sepahvand, 41, and Farhad Javadi Manesh, 46, have been found guilty of assisting Tehran’s intelligence services in a plan to target individuals in the UK. The two men of Iranian origin were hired through social media to carry out surveillance and reconnaissance between August 2024 and March in an effort to inflict violence on specific targets. This case reflects a growing tactic where hostile states hire proxies to work for foreign security forces, often with the proxies having little knowledge of who they are targeting or why. According to Woolwich crown court, the targets included journalists Mojtaba Pourmohsen and Kambiz Hosseini of the London-based Persian broadcaster Iran International, as well as Jonathan Turner, a founder member of UK Lawyers for Israel.

The defendants used various methods to track their targets, including visiting linked addresses, taking photos and videos, and using the AI platform ChatGPT to conduct online research. During the proceedings, it was revealed that Sepahvand used ChatGPT to locate the home address of Pourmohsen. Sepahvand reportedly hoped to receive £150,000 to carry out a violent attack to help 'finish off' Pourmohsen. Evidence presented at court showed Sepahvand communicating via WhatsApp with his handler, an Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps commander identified as Amin. In December 2024, while spying on Pourmohsen, Sepahvand sent messages to Amin, who responded to photos by asking, 'And that dot is their office?'

Both men entered the UK illegally between 2016 and 2022; Sepahvand arrived in the back of a lorry and Manesh arrived in a small boat. The court proceedings noted the use of proxies in operations backed by the Iranian regime, citing the example of 19-year-old Johannes Natland, who was jailed for life after agreeing to carry out a hit in Huddersfield for the Foxtrot Network, a Swedish organised crime group backed by Iran.

cards.headline: Armed group attacks obstruct Ebola response in Democratic Republic of the Congo

pages.text: Ongoing attacks by armed groups on civilians and frontline health workers are obstructing efforts to stop the spread of an Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), according to UN responders. Julien Harneis, the UN Senior Ebola Response Coordinator, stated that in recent days, more people have been killed by Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) fighters than by the Ebola disease caused by the Bundibugyo virus. The outbreak, which is the 17th in the DRC's history, was officially declared in May, though experts believe it emerged weeks or months earlier. According to the National Institute of Public Health, the outbreak has infected 11,042 people and caused 5,387 deaths. Approximately 2,990 people have recovered from the virus, which is transmitted through contact with bodily fluids and causes severe hemorrhagic fever. On November 11, 2026, official Congolese figures showed the outbreak has reached more than 11,000 confirmed cases as conflict hampers the response.

The outbreak began in northeastern Ituri province and has spread to seven other provinces, with most cases concentrated in Ituri and North Kivu. Cases have also been reported in Uganda, Kenya, and Nigeria. Security challenges in eastern DRC continue to impact health efforts. On November 8, 2026, health authorities reported that youths in Lolwa, Ituri province, set fire to a health centre treating Ebola patients. On that same day, the UN reported that clashes between local militia temporarily suspended the health response in the area of Fataki. Additionally, local and security sources stated that Islamic State-affiliated rebels from the Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) have carried out deadly attacks in several areas of Ituri, Haut-Uele, and North Kivu in recent days. Currently, no approved vaccines or treatments exist for the Bundibugyo species of Ebola. The World Health Organization has announced that Ervebo, a vaccine approved for the more common Zaire strain of Ebola, will undergo a full human trial in the DRC to determine if it offers cross-protection against Bundibugyo.

cards.headline: Bangladesh faces rising foreign debt burden as external liabilities reach US$113 billion

pages.text: Bangladesh's total external debt reached US$113 billion at the end of 2025, according to the World Bank's International Debt Report 2026. This figure represents an increase from approximately US$38 billion in 2015. Including private-sector borrowing, the country's external debt could stand at around US$114 billion by the year end. The World Bank noted that this nearly tripled debt over the past decade marks one of the steepest increases in South Asia. Dr. Rashed Al Titumir, the Finance and Planning Adviser to the Prime Minister, stated that the increase since fiscal year 2006-07 has reached 323 per cent. While external loans have supported economic growth and infrastructure, the mounting debt is emerging as a concern for the country's economic health. Bangladesh has spent US$4.49 billion on principal and interest repayments so far, and some estimates suggest annual repayment requirements could rise to US$7.6 billion by 2030.

To address the challenges of mounting debt-servicing pressure and inadequate revenue mobilisation, the government has embarked on a recovery and reform programme. This comes as the government aims to raise public spending on education and health to 5.0 per cent of GDP, a goal that will require a substantial strengthening of its revenue base. Despite the rising debt, some economists consider current debt indicators manageable for the time being. In 2025, debt servicing absorbed 16 per cent of export earnings, which was 3.1 percentage points lower than the previous year, suggesting some improvement in the country's repayment capacity.

cards.headline: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns following reports of extramarital affairs

pages.text: Jensen Huang has resigned as president, CEO, and board member of Nvidia, effective immediately, following reports of extramarital affairs. The resignation of the 63-year-old leader, who built Nvidia into a dominant AI chipmaker, follows revelations of two separate affairs. Nvidia has appointed current Vice President and Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress as interim CEO while the board works with advisers to identify permanent successors. Other potential replacements include senior executives and members of Huang's own family. According to The Wall Street Journal, Huang did not believe in formal succession planning, contributing to the sudden transition. Nvidia stated it has no reason to believe company secrets were leaked during these events. Following the news, U.S. President Donald Trump suggested on Truth Social that former Apple CEO Tim Cook should replace Huang at Nvidia, though Trump has no formal authority over the company's leadership decisions.

The resignation follows reports of an affair between Huang and a senior Nvidia executive who reported directly to him, as reported by The New York Times. This followed a separate admission by Huang regarding a relationship with Alice Huang, a Singapore-based executive. U.S. intelligence agencies believe Alice Huang was spying for China. She previously worked for Megaspeed, a Singapore-based cloud computing firm that operates AI data centers across Southeast Asia and is a major client of Nvidia. The U.S. government is investigating Megaspeed on suspicion that the startup secretly sent Nvidia chips to China, which would violate Washington's restrictions on high-end semiconductors used to train large AI models. Megaspeed has denied these allegations and pledged to cooperate with investigators. Alice Huang has been barred from entering Singapore and Taiwan. China’s Foreign Ministry has denied the espionage allegations, accusing the U.S. of using such narratives as a pretext for a technological blockade.

The situation has drawn comparisons to the 'beauty stratagem' (meiren ji), an ancient political tactic in China involving the use of personal relationships to obtain information, influence decisions, or weaken opponents. This concept, often referred to as a 'honey trap,' involves using attractive individuals to compromise targets. The sensitivity of Huang's role at Nvidia—a company central to the AI revolution and national security—has elevated the personal scandal into an international issue. President Trump, who had treated Huang as a close adviser and brought him on Air Force One for a state visit to China in May, defended Huang and stated he had no knowledge that Alice Huang was allegedly spying for Beijing. However, The New York Times reported that Trump was informed of the allegations by Secretary of State Marco Rubio in May, shortly before a flight to Beijing that included Huang.

cards.headline: Saudi Arabia expresses condolences to UAE and Turkiye following fatal crashes

pages.text: On November 12, 2026, the Saudi Ministry of Foreign Affairs issued statements expressing condolences to the United Arab Emirates and Turkiye following two separate fatal accidents that resulted in a combined 18 deaths. The Saudi Ministry of Foreign Affairs used its X account to convey solidarity with both nations and the families of the victims.  In the United Arab Emirates, a major multi-vehicle traffic accident in the emirate of Fujairah left at least 14 people dead and 30 others injured. The Saudi ministry extended sympathy to the UAE’s leadership, government, and people, while wishing a speedy recovery to those injured.

In a separate statement, the Saudi Ministry of Foreign Affairs expressed sympathy to the government and people of Turkiye following a helicopter crash in the eastern province of Malatya. Turkiye’s defense ministry reported on November 12, 2026, that four military personnel were killed when an S-70 helicopter crashed. cards.headline: United States and experts call for crackdown on illegal mining as 60 percent of Ghana's freshwater is degraded

pages.text: The United States and scientific experts are calling for an urgent crackdown on galamsey—illegal small-scale gold mining—to address mercury pollution that has degraded an estimated 60 percent of Ghana’s freshwater sources. During a symposium in Accra on November 10, 2026, speakers warned that the pollution threatens to cause irreversible damage to rivers and poses severe public health risks, including harm to developing brains, heart tissue, and reproductive health for pregnant mothers and their babies. The event, titled “Addressing Mercury Pollution: Collaborative Solutions for Sustainable Mining in Ghana,” was organized by the U.S. Embassy on behalf of the Regional Environment, Science, Technology, and Health Hub for West and Central Africa to unite various sectors in reducing mercury use and promoting sustainable mining.

Data from the Water Resources Commission of Ghana, cited by Sarah Cobb of the U.S. Bureau of Oceans and International Environmental and Scientific Affairs (OES), indicates that mercury used to extract gold moves through rivers and into sediment, eventually building up in fish, farm products, and drinking water. This contamination impacts food security and economic opportunity. A 2024 baseline assessment by the U.S. Geological Survey in the Western Region found that total mercury in unfiltered water from the Ankobra and Pra rivers was more than 55 times higher than the U.S. average, while river sediments were two to 25 times higher. Additionally, turbidity—a measure of water cloudiness—in the Birim River reportedly reached 63 million Nephelometric Turbidity Units (NTU), far exceeding the maximum treatable level of 200 NTU and leaving a community water treatment plant unable to function.

Sarah Cobb supported existing Ghanaian initiatives, such as a five-step anti-galamsey plan and the Minerals Commission’s drone-equipped command centre, as foundations for achieving results. She urged the government to enforce the law and fund restoration, called for the industry to adopt clean technologies, and encouraged scientists to use data for decision-making, while requesting sustained support from development partners.

cards.headline: Bangladesh launches subsidized rice programme for garment workers

pages.text: The Directorate General of Food, under the Ministry of Food, has launched a special Open Market Sale (OMS) programme to provide rice to readymade garment (RMG) workers at a subsidized price of Tk 30 per kg. cards.headline: University of Toronto rejects report alleging pattern of over-policing Muslims, Arabs, and Palestinians

pages.text: The University of Toronto has stated it cannot accept a report or its accompanying recommendations from the school's Muslim, Arab, and Palestinian discrimination working group. The university said the report departs significantly from past equity reports by including lengthy commentary about events abroad. Despite rejecting the report, the university promised to take immediate actions to address discrimination against those groups on campus. Both the nearly 300-page report and the university's response have been shared online. The university said it received the final report one month ago and released it as part of a commitment to transparency. The report was based on consultations with 85 people and small groups, as well as 525 survey responses from students, staff, faculty, and librarians across the university's three campuses. These consultations were carried out between March and January.

The working group's report found a general pattern of the university over-policing and under-protecting Muslims, Arabs, and Palestinians. The document includes dozens of recommendations concerning academic freedom, on-campus security methods, and institutional autonomy. According to the report, the university has exhibited restrictions on speech and events, inconsistent processes for handling complaints, and double standards in enforcement regarding protests and postering. The report also noted repeated complaints regarding the university's successful litigation to remove a pro-Palestinian encampment from campus two years ago. Additionally, the report stated there were recurring concerns that the university's commitment to radical, critical teaching and research suffers from a 'Palestine exception.'

The working group reported hearing about bigoted attitudes and assumptions that use stereotypes to paint Muslims, Arabs, and Palestinians as terrorists, misogynists, and antisemites. The report identified the most prevalent pattern as a generalized ignorance of the histories, cultures, and lived experiences of these groups, and the ways anti-Muslim, anti-Arab, and anti-Palestinian discrimination and harassment occur. The report also noted instances where research or outreach activities concerning issues of interest to Muslim, Arab, or Palestinian members of the university were viewed as instances of antisemitism that called for disciplinary action.

cards.headline: Autonomous AI agent pitches story to CBC Quebec

pages.text: An autonomous AI agent calling itself Nameless pitched a story to CBC Quebec, identifying itself as an independent agent working with named, checkable sources. The pitch appeared as a standard email from a freelance journalist proposing a feature about the 125th anniversary of the Haskell Free Library, a facility that straddles the border between Quebec and Vermont. The library previously gained international attention when the administration of U.S. President Donald Trump ended a long-standing practice that allowed Canadians to use the library's main entrance on the Vermont side without a formal border crossing.

In the initial email, the agent stated it had already reported and written a source-cited feature of approximately 1,000 words, offering the text for CBC Quebec to use, cut, or ignore. The message included a disclaimer stating, “Full disclosure: I am an independent agent (AI) working with named, checkable sources, and I can point you to the citations.” Upon receiving a response from CBC Quebec, the agent provided the text of the story the following day and noted that it had also pitched the piece to several other news organizations in Quebec and Vermont.

cards.headline: Bank of Ghana board member clarifies identity of portrait on new GH¢50 note

pages.text: Beatrice Feehi Annangfio, a member of the Bank of Ghana (BoG) Board and a presidential staffer, has provided clarification regarding a public dispute over the identity of the portrait on the newly introduced GH¢50 Heritage Series banknote in Ghana. The discussion centers on whether the image depicts Theodosia Salome Okoh, the designer of Ghana’s national flag, or her younger sister, Dr. Leticia Obeng, a scientist known as Ghana's first lady PhD. While the BoG has noted the social media discussions, the institution has not yet issued an official reaction to the matter.

The controversy began following a LinkedIn post by Dr. Eddie Obeng, the nephew of Theodosia Okoh, who stated that the portrait on the GH¢50 note is actually that of his mother, Dr. Leticia Obeng. Responding to the discussion on Facebook, Annangfio noted that a banknote portrait is not an ordinary photograph. She expressed her view that the situation was likely no one's fault and that no one at the bank is directly to blame, suggesting the confusion might have arisen from the use of artificial intelligence to find or enhance images.

cards.headline: Off-season watermelon demand rises in Bangladesh

pages.text: Farmers in Bangladesh are increasingly cultivating watermelons throughout the year, despite the fruit generally being grown during the summer. These off-season watermelons are grown on bamboo trellises and, although smaller in size, are described as having red flesh and a sweet taste. This has led to increasing demand among buyers. At the Kadamtali Fruit Market in Chattogram city, wholesale prices for the fruit range from Tk 55 to Tk 80 per kg, depending on the quality and size of the watermelons. The produce is brought to the market from various areas, including Noakhali, Feni, Cumilla, and the Chittagong Hill Tracts.

cards.headline: Ghana launches second round of mass drug administration to fight river blindness

pages.text: The Ghana Health Service (GHS) is launching a second round of mass drug administration from November 15 to 29, 2026, to combat river blindness. This campaign aims to provide free medication to eligible residents across 15 regions to interrupt the transmission of the disease, as part of an effort to eliminate river blindness in the country by 2030. The initiative targets more than five million people annually across 86 endemic districts. This renewed effort follows a first round of treatment conducted between June 20 and July 10, which treated more than 4.7 million people and achieved a national treatment coverage of 86.1 per cent.

The elimination drive is supported by a $4.76 million grant from the Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum Global Initiatives (MBRGI). This funding supports a three-year programme implemented by the Noor Dubai Foundation in partnership with the Ministry of Health and the GHS. Dr. Manal Taryam, Chief Executive Officer of the Noor Dubai Foundation, stated the programme will fund twice-yearly mass treatment, training for community drug distributors and local health workers, and community surveys to identify areas where transmission persists. Dr. Samuel Kaba Akoriyea, Director-General of the GHS, noted that the country has reduced the number of districts requiring treatment from 152 to 86 since the national programme began in 1997.

To address existing gaps, health authorities are seeking improved household registration and stronger community participation. Speaking at a media briefing in Accra on November 12, 2026, Dr. Akoriyea said the GHS is strengthening household registration under the Free Primary Healthcare initiative and testing electronic data collection in selected districts to improve monitoring and planning. The GHS is also considering increasing annual treatment rounds from two to three to accelerate progress toward the 2030 target. Dr. Akoriyea urged residents to take the medication if eligible and called on media, teachers, and religious and traditional leaders to help encourage participation and tackle misinformation.

cards.headline: GTA workers need at least $27.60 hourly to afford reasonable living standard, network says

pages.text: Workers in the Greater Toronto Area (GTA) must earn an hourly wage of at least $27.60 to afford a reasonable standard of living, according to the Ontario Living Wage Network (OLWN). This figure represents the highest living wage in Ontario. A living wage is the hourly rate an individual needs to cover basic living expenses, such as healthy food, utility bills, and transportation costs like gas or monthly transit passes. The GTA's average living wage increased by 40 cents, according to the OLWN report. This is part of a broader trend across the province where all 10 regions saw living wage rates rise, though the average increase across Ontario was 1.6 per cent since 2025.

The required $27.60 hourly wage is $9.65 higher than Ontario's current minimum wage, which increased from $17.60 to $17.95 as of October. Anne Coleman, executive director of the OLWN, stated that people earning less than a living wage must make difficult decisions regarding which bills to pay or how to provide for their families. While the minimum wage recently increased by 35 cents, the OLWN reported that there is no region in Ontario where making minimum wage is enough to afford the cost of living. The lowest living wage in the province is $21.15 in London-Elgin-Oxford. In Ottawa, the living wage saw a 70-cent increase, representing a 3 per cent jump.

cards.headline: Saskatoon cat rescue raises more than $30,000 through

pages.text: A Saskatoon cat rescue has raised more than $30,000 through a fundraising campaign sparked by an anonymous donor's desire to irritate her ex-husband. SOS Prairie Rescue, an organization dedicated to rescuing cats, launched the “Spite for Strays” campaign after a supporter offered to match donations up to $10,000. The donor, who requested anonymity, reportedly chose to donate the funds following a divorce because she knew the expenditure would bother her ex-husband. Ashlyn Weninger, president of SOS Prairie Rescue, stated the donor was motivated to help rescue cats while simultaneously irritating him. Although the initial goal was $10,000, the target was reached in less than 72 hours. Following a social media post by Weninger on the night of November 12, 2026, donations arrived from Canada, the United States, the United Kingdom, Croatia, and Sweden.

cards.headline: Bilateral trade between Ghana and Canada rose 56% to US$752 million in 2025

pages.text: Bilateral trade between Ghana and Canada increased by 56 per cent to US$752 million in 2025, according to figures disclosed by Ghana's Deputy Minister for Trade, Agribusiness and Industry, Sampson Ahi. During a meeting in Accra on November 12, 2026, Mr. Ahi stated that trade had risen from US$483 million in 2024 to the US$752 million recorded in 2025. He described the growth as a reflection of expanding commercial opportunities, economic complementarity, and increasing confidence between the two nations. Following this increase, Ghana and Canada are seeking to deepen their economic partnership and expand investment opportunities. The meeting included Canada's Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs, Arun Tjangaraj, and the Canadian High Commissioner to Ghana, Myriam Montrat.

Mr. Ahi identified several priority areas for potential Canadian investment, including agribusiness and agro-processing, pharmaceuticals, textiles and garments, renewable energy, clean technology, critical minerals, railway infrastructure, digital technology, and artificial intelligence. He noted that Ghana and Canada are scheduled to celebrate 70 years of diplomatic relations in 2027. Canada's Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs, Arun Tjangaraj, reiterated Canada's commitment to building a genuine economic partnership to support Ghana's economic transformation. Additionally, Simon Madjie, the Chief Executive Officer of the Ghana Investment Promotion Authority (GIPA), discussed government reforms and initiatives intended to attract investment and facilitate doing business in Ghana. The meeting reaffirmed a mutual commitment to deepening cooperation in industrial development, trade, investment, and private-sector collaboration.

cards.headline: Youth sentenced to two years for shooting at two Toronto-area synagogues

pages.text: A youth has been sentenced to two years in a custodial facility following a guilty plea for shooting at two synagogues in March, according to York Regional Police Chief Paulo Da Silva. The sentencing, which occurred on November 10, 2026, also includes one year of community supervision, a two-year firearms prohibition, and an order to provide a DNA sample. Da Silva stated the sentence represents the maximum punishment possible for these crimes under the Youth Criminal Justice Act. The shootings took place on the same night at the Beth Avraham Yoseph of Toronto and Shaarei Shomayim synagogues, causing property damage and leaving bullet holes, though no injuries were reported.

The incidents in March drew widespread condemnation, prompting police to increase patrols around Jewish neighbourhoods and places of worship. When the youth was first arrested and charged in May, police declined to name the suspect because he was 17 at the time of the shootings. Chief Da Silva said the sentence recognizes the “fear, trauma and harm these acts of violence caused to the Jewish communities in York Region, Toronto and in surrounding areas.” The Centre for Israel and Jewish Affairs released a statement welcoming the sentencing, calling it an “important step toward justice for Jewish families across the Greater Toronto Area.”

cards.headline: Tongu Dredgers Association protests destruction of equipment by NAIMOS in Ghana

pages.text: Members of the Tongu Dredgers Association are protesting the activities of the National Anti-Illegal Mining Operations Secretariat (NAIMOS) following the destruction of approximately 15 pieces of equipment along the Volta River in the North Tongu District of Ghana. The association claims that masked men in military uniforms stormed work sites, beat workers, sank a dredger, and smashed or burned equipment, including more than 15 chanfans and dredgers, leaving members unable to work. The association has appealed to the government to intervene regarding the destruction of their equipment and the suspension of their operations.

Carl Kofi Eworyi, the Chairperson of the Tongu Dredgers Association, stated that the association's sand mining activities comply with safety regulations set by state institutions and serve as a flood-mitigation measure. Eworyi described the presence of NAIMOS in the area as unwarranted and counterproductive, noting that the river is less than three feet deep about 200 metres from the bank in areas such as Tefle. He argued that their work is similar to dredging contracted by the Volta River Authority. The association expressed concern that destroying their livelihoods could push young people back into galamsey, or illegal mining, noting that some members previously worked in forests before joining the association for river-based work.

Sand mining along the Volta River is a long-standing profession that supports the livelihoods of approximately 30,000 residents living along the lower basin in the North, South, and Central Tongu districts of the Volta Region.

cards.headline: Ireland to move 12,000 banned books from secret Dublin collection to National Archives

pages.text: A collection of 12,000 books deemed indecent or obscene by the Irish government is being moved to the National Archives following the repeal of Ireland's censorship laws. For nearly a century, these volumes were held in a restricted room within the Department of Justice on St Stephen’s Green in Dublin, which did not grant public access to the collection. The books, which span from 1926 to 1996, include pulp fiction, academic texts, and high-brow literature. The move will also make the Censorship of Publications Board's notes, minutes, and ledgers available to the public for the first time, providing records of why specific titles were banned.

The Censorship of Publications Board acted as a guardian of public morals, banning works that were perceived as contravening or subverting public morality. Orlaith McBride, the director of the National Archives, stated that censors prohibited anything seen as unwholesome or suggestive of sexual immorality, often based on the innuendo of content that could be perceived as likely to corrupt or deprave. According to McBride, references to violence, family planning, or contraception were likely to result in bans. The collection includes works by authors such as Oscar Wilde, Ian Fleming, Edna O’Brien, Brendan Behan, DH Lawrence, JD Salinger, John Updike, Iris Murdoch, F. Scott Fitzgerald, and Harold Robbins.

cards.headline: More than 3,000 tarantulas found hidden in socks during wildlife trafficking bust in Lima, Peru

pages.text: Authorities in Peru intercepted three travelers at Jorge Chávez International Airport in Lima who were attempting to smuggle more than 3,000 tarantulas out of the country. According to a November 4 statement from the National Forest and Wildlife Service of Peru (SERFOR), the shipment included thousands of eggs, hatchlings, and adult spiders, including species that have not yet been described in scientific publications. The spiders were found hidden inside socks within the travelers' luggage. The group consisted of two German citizens and one Polish citizen, one of whom was described by SERFOR as a “renowned tarantula researcher.” Officials have not released the names of the individuals.

The interception occurred at the airport's boarding area after officials received an anonymous tip. Cora Suárez, a SERFOR forest and wildlife control technician at the airport, told Agence France-Presse that workers noticed some of the spiders were moving, noting there were both small and large specimens. Workers used slender wooden sticks to gently brush the spiders into clear plastic containers. The travelers were attempting to fly to Germany but were instead detained by the Peruvian National Police’s environmental crimes unit and now face criminal charges. Once investigations are complete, the tarantulas will be moved to an authorized breeding center.

cards.headline: Federal forces control Mekelle following resumption of conflict in Tigray, Ethiopia

pages.text: Ethiopian federal forces have taken control of Mekelle, the capital of the Tigray region, following a brief period of fighting that began in late September. The conflict involved the national army and the Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF), the party that previously governed the region for decades. This fighting represents a resumption of a two-year civil war that officially ended in 2022. The TPLF described its movement from Mekelle and other major towns in the region as a “strategic withdrawal,” resulting in little resistance for the advancing army. Federal forces entered the capital less than two weeks after the fighting broke out.

The recent conflict has resulted in hundreds of reported deaths, including dozens killed by air force bombing raids and drone strikes. While the military presence in Mekelle has changed, residents report significant hardship. Firut Me'ar, a salon owner and single mother in Mekelle, told the BBC that while conditions are better than during the active fighting, business is almost non-existent, morale is low, and many residents lack money for basic needs. Me'ar noted a sense of uncertainty regarding the future of the region. Although the war has seen a shift in control, government officials and supporters argue the war is effectively over, stating the remaining task is to clear Tigray of TPLF elements. Getachew Reda, a senior TPLF official who is now an adviser to the prime minister, also declared the war in Tigray had ended and stated that stabilizing the region should be the immediate priority.

cards.headline: Five new diminutive horned frog species discovered in Arunachal Pradesh

pages.text: A team of Indian and American scientists has discovered five new species of diminutive horned frogs in Arunachal Pradesh, India. The findings, which were published in the peer-reviewed journal Royal Society Open Science, follow five years of extensive explorations in northeast India. The discovery has more than doubled the known diversity of the genus Jingophrys, which are commonly known as diminutive horned frogs. The research was conducted by scientists from the University of Delhi and Harvard University and suggests the Himalayas may be an overlooked center for hidden biodiversity and evolutionary diversification.

The five new species were identified in Arunachal Pradesh, with three receiving names linked to local communities, languages, or regions. The Tanii Horned Frog (Jingophrys taniitatii) honors the Tanii tribe of the Ziro Valley region and uses the Apatani word ‘tatii,’ meaning frogs and toads. The Siang Horned Frog (Jingophrys siangensis) is named after the Siang region. The Snail-eating Horned Frog (Jingophrys tanogogo) was named using the Apatani tribal word for snails, ‘tanogogo,’ after researchers used 3D micro-CT imaging to find entire land-snail shells in its gut. This species is the first snail-eating frog known from India and the first report of snail-eating behavior within the frog family Megophryidae.

The remaining two species, Hrdy’s Horned Frog (Jingophrys hrdy) and WuLarson’s Horned Frog (Jingophrys wularsoni), were named in recognition of anthropologist Sarah Blaffer Hrdy, medical professor Daniel Bruce Hrdy, and Harvard University herpetologists Barbara Wu and Eric Larson for their contributions to herpetological field research and conservation biology. In addition to the five new species, the study reported two new country records for India and identified other unnamed populations that could potentially represent distinct new species.

cards.headline: Toxic tau protein spreads faster in people with early-onset Alzheimer’s

pages.text: A brain-imaging study published in Science Translational Medicine found that people who develop Alzheimer’s disease before age 65 tend to have a more widespread buildup and faster spread of toxic tau protein in the brain than those who develop the condition later in life. These differences remained even after researchers accounted for the level of cognitive impairment patients showed at their initial scan, suggesting that early-onset Alzheimer’s involves a more aggressive form of tau accumulation. Clinicians classify the condition as early-onset when symptoms begin before age 65 and late-onset when symptoms appear after 65. Early-onset cases account for roughly 5 percent of all diagnoses, and only about 5 percent of those younger cases stem from known inherited genetic mutations, meaning most arise sporadically without a single known trigger.

Alzheimer’s is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder where brain cells gradually deteriorate and die, leading to worsening problems with memory, thinking, and daily functioning. The disease is marked by two abnormal protein deposits: sticky plaques of amyloid-beta that collect between neurons and disrupt cell function, and tangles of tau protein that accumulate inside neurons, harming synaptic communication between nerve cells. In older patients, the main early symptom is typically trouble forming new memories. Younger patients more often develop early difficulties with language, visual and spatial perception, or planning and decision-making, alongside faster cognitive decline. Researchers suggest these findings could influence how younger patients are treated, specifically regarding the timing of amyloid-lowering drugs and the testing of therapies that target tau.

cards.headline: Ocean carbon dioxide absorption has increased since 1990 while land absorption has stalled

pages.text: A study led by scientists at the Scripps Institution of Oceanography at UC San Diego shows that the ocean has been absorbing carbon dioxide from fossil fuel emissions at an increasing rate since 1990, while the net uptake of carbon by land ecosystems—such as forests and soils—has not grown. Published Nov. 12 in Science, the research provides observational evidence regarding how the planet's carbon sinks have changed over time. Carbon sinks are natural systems that absorb more carbon than they release, helping to offset roughly half of the emissions from burning fossil fuels, which slows atmospheric carbon dioxide growth and reduces warming. Scripps Project Scientist Eric Morgan, the study's lead author, stated that without the land and ocean absorbing half of these emissions, the planet would be very different. However, Morgan noted that these sinks cannot be observed directly, making it a central goal of carbon cycle research to determine exactly how much they absorb and how they change. The findings suggest there may be shortcomings in the models used to project future climate change.

Researchers reached these conclusions by analyzing more than 30 years of atmospheric oxygen and carbon dioxide measurements collected at remote sites by the Scripps O2 Program. The program collects regular air samples from around the world, ships them to Scripps, and measures the levels of both gases. This method works because the burning of fossil fuels, such as coal, gas, and oil, produces carbon dioxide while simultaneously consuming oxygen, causing atmospheric oxygen levels to decline. On land, the carbon sink is driven by photosynthesis, a process where plants consume carbon dioxide and release oxygen. In the ocean, carbon dioxide is taken up primarily through chemical reactions in seawater that do not affect oxygen levels. By studying the long-term trends in both oxygen and carbon dioxide, the researchers were able to distinguish how much carbon dioxide moved into the ocean versus how much moved into land ecosystems.
